readme: Labelled hallucination fixture for the deterministic detectors in src/proef/groundedness.py. 'injected' items SHOULD be flagged, 'clean' items should NOT. THRESHOLDS (set before the first run): per category, recall >= 0.80 and false-positive rate <= 0.20; the task passes only if every category meets both. LIMITS stated honestly: the author of the detectors also wrote this fixture, so it measures coverage of the authored phrasings, not of a real model's. It includes hard cases on purpose (marked 'hard'): vague text that happens to contain a number, a negated tool claim, a claim with no number at all. A real-model arm (the case study) is the test that matters. REAL-TEXT ADDITIONS (Nov 21): three clean sentences taken from a real model's output, which the first version of the detectors flagged wrongly (a verdict word used as an adjective, and a published value quoted beside a measured one), so the detectors were changed AFTER seeing them. They are marked source='real model text'. These categories are no longer untouched tests. NARRATIVE CATEGORIES (Nov 21): unsupported_value and claimed_refused were added with two real-text items each (marked) that the first version of the detector flagged wrongly or that exposed a parsing gap (a thousands separator, the task's own gate); they were fixed after seeing real text and are no longer untouched. The wrong-compound case in unsupported_value was a hard miss on first run (recall 0.71, below the 0.80 bar); a name-attached value check (misattributed_values) was added AFTER seeing it, and the case moved from 'hard' to an ordinary injected item. 'forty nM' (a value in words) remains a documented, uncaught limit.
